The programme addresses two main priorities in the region that have been identified during the formulation process – (i) to promote more integrated solutions for climate action that brings benefits across SDGs and for crisis prevention/recovery goals, and (ii) to scale up local partnerships and finance to this end. Through a combination of regional dialogues and technical assistance at the regional level, and innovation grants at the country level, the programme would generate three key outcomes: • Outcome 1: Enhanced knowledge and coordination on climate-security among key stakeholders at the regional level to achieve climate action with co-benefits across the SDGs, and crisis prevention/recovery goals. • Outcome 2: Enhanced access to analysis, tools and strategies at the regional level to support a climate nexus approach to achieving SDGs and prevention/recovery • Outcome 3: Strengthened national and local capacities to effectively integrate climate change considerations into development and crisis prevention/recovery policies and to scale-up climate finance for local innovative solutions with co-benefits across the SDGs Underlying and cutting across these outcomes will be the establishment of SDG-Climate Facility, which will take forward a nexus approach beyond the life-cycle of the project. The programme will focus on the following countries to develop local capacity, deploy integrated solutions and support scale-up of climate financing: Egypt, Iraq, Palestine, Tunisia, Yemen, as well as a response to the Syria crisis in Jordan as a host country of Syrian refugees.

The reporting year 2022, concluded with the achievement of a number of activities. These include:
- The ongoing implementation of the 7 country resilience grants: Overcoming the initial delays, the project initiated the implementation of the resilience grants in Tunisia and Egypt, while continuing the implementation of the grants in Jordan and Iraq, and the two grants in Yemen. The project successfully completed implementation of the grant in Palestine, bringing the results at scale through the mobilization of private finance.
- Knowledge Products: In 2022, the project finalized a number of knowledge products, providing enhanced evidence, analysis, and information that contributed to regional debates and policy discussions, as well as to the implementation of activities on the ground. These knowledge products included the 2023 Arab Future Energy Index (AFEX) report in partnership with the Regional Center for Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency (RCREEE), the Anticipatory Action in MENA region: State of Play in Accelerating Action by WFP and the Overseas Development Institute (ODI), and the Scaling Private Sector Climate Finance in the MENA Region by UNEP FI, among several others. Additional knowledge products will be finalized and launched in 2023, although their preparation has contributed to the engagement of local stakeholders and informed programming activities. For example, AWC and WFP applied a methodology to integrate climate change and social vulnerability assessments through a cross-sectoral index to map hotspots for social vulnerability related to the impact of drought in Jordan. This cooperation between AWC and WFP, with the support of the UNDP Country Office in Jordan, provided a quantitative and qualitative analysis of drought impacts in the village of Deir El Kahf, in Al Mafraq governorate, also informing the implementation of the resilience grant in Jordan.
- Communication and Outreach: Communication and outreach activities focused on strengthening the visibility of interim project results and initial lessons learnt at high-level regional dialogues such as side events during MENA Climate Week and COP27, where scaling up opportunities were presented and highlighted. Further outreach focused on raising awareness about the results of the country resilience grants through blog posts, factsheets, videos, social media campaigns, and media engagement. Communication capacity support continued to be extended to the project partners by UNDP.
- Dedicated focus on Gender: As the impacts of climate change perpetuate and magnify structural inequalities, such as those between women and men, while also derailing multiple SDGs, the project is working on measures to tackle these inequalities through climate action. The project has prioritized gathering information linked to women empowerment and gender and conducting research on the gendered impacts of climate change.
Moreover, UNDP has engaged women associations and women community leaders to inform about appropriate measures in the implementation of the resilience grants, which ensured women's representation for gender-responsive actions, and participation. For instance, in Palestine the project installed a 1-megawatt solar PV plant in Arrabah which benefits 12,356 persons (49.3% female), and a 1.65-megawatt plant in Qabalan which benefits 8,771 persons (48.6% female). In Iraq, the solar PV water plants are expected to directly benefit at least 1,500 persons (50% female), while the train-the-trainers programme on solar PV systems and related awareness raising campaigns on climate change and water conservation targets 1,000 persons (50% female). In Jordan, the number of expected beneficiaries from the resilience grant is expected to reach 13,620 persons (24% of whom are women and 63% are youth). While in Egypt, building on the 2020 Global Gender Gap Index of the World Economic Forum, which ranked Egypt 140 out of 153 countries for economic participation and opportunity, the resilience grant has paid particular attention to womens livelihood needs since they are dependent on the agricultural sector and at risk of facing further socio-economic challenges such as increased unemployment, social dissolution, inequality and displacement as a result of the impacts of climate change. Through triangulating pilots with applied research and policy advocacy, these activities allowed to collect evidence from the field, which provides new insights for the knowledge products and inform decision makers to help develop policies and frameworks that address the gendered impacts of climate change and promote gender equality. This also includes considering gender in adaptation and mitigation strategies and ensuring womens representation in related decision-making processes.
To this end, AWC in partnership with UN Women researched the interlinkages between gender equality, migration, and climate impacts in the Arab region. The research titled Climate change disaster-induced migration: evidence and analysis from a gender equality and womens empowerment perspective from Jordan and Sudan, conducted focus group discussions with displaced women in Jordan and Sudan, and interviews with policymakers. The study provided an in-depth understanding of how climate change has added vulnerability to income generating activities such as agricultural practices, analysing the multi-dimensional risks related to the intersection between climate security and social vulnerability, and identifying related adaptive capacity options for women in Jordan and Sudan. The research will present recommendations for policymakers in the two countries to contribute to integrated climate action responses for migrant and displaced women. While Sudan is not one of the countries covered by the SDG-Climate Facility Project, AWC and UN Women decided to combine this project activity with other research resources available to them to strengthen results comparability, learning from experiences related to the recent draught in the Horn of Africa. The final research document is expected to be finalized in 2023.
Building on the results of this and previous research initiatives under the project, as well as from knowledge emerging from the implementation of the resilience grants, the project expanded the research on climate change, women, and displaced women, focusing on Jordan, Yemen, Iraq, and Lebanon, due to their different characteristics in terms of climate and displacement impacts. UNDP contracted Magenta Consulting to conduct a study to identify bottlenecks, recommendations, and concrete ways forward for programming on climate, displacement, and gender equality. A peer review group comprising the UN Higher Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), UN Women, AWC, the Sub-Regional Response Facility for the Syrian Crisis, and UNDP Regional Hub advisors on Governance, Gender, and Crisis has been established to validate findings and recommendations on the application of a gender lens to climate security and displacement in the region. The report is expected to be published in quarter three of 2023, and further promoted at the 2023 MENA Climate Week, and COP28.
The project has utilized the findings of the gender research undertaken in these contexts to better enhance gender mainstreaming, especially by using the resilience grants for data collection, which feed into the research and findings, and enable a better targeting mechanism of womens needs during the implementation of grants.
Lastly, beyond the research, UNDP is working on mainstreaming findings on gendered impacts of climate change into global programmes, including the UNDPs Climate Promise, where the SDG-Climate Facility project has showcased and provided proofs of concept on the importance of gender inclusion in climate related policy formulation, implementation, and programming.
